comments.author: pdkl95
comments.story_title: Things the media does to manufacture outrage
comments.why_zh: 解释网络名气如何降临到人身上，以及受众如何反应。
comments.quote_zh: 关于这类关系变化的极佳解释，我建议去看《This is Phil Fish》[4]。
comments.text_zh: TL;DR——直接去看 [4]。互联网在名气这件事上有严重的毛病。在互联网之前，名气通常需要你在媒体渠道上有所投入。人人都知道那部好莱坞大片，是因为他们砸了大笔钱做广告等等。一部低预算的电影如果人们知道它，可能潜力更大，但微薄（或根本不存在）的广告预算通常保证了它永远不会[1]出名。这就是互联网改变的东西。它的根本力量在于任何人都能发布，因为网络并不区分"发布"主机和"消费"主机。所有对等节点在能力上都应该是[2]平等的。互联网就是媒体渠道。过去需要投入大量时间和/或金钱的事，如今在人们随手在网上发点东西时就经常发生：他们可以出名。不幸的是，我们的社会规范还在适应这个变化。正如这篇文章所示，琐碎的帖子被错误地解读，作者最终只能在火焰和辱骂中跋涉。这是因为，原本只是一条随手的帖子，现在却在对着一群受众说话。关于这类关系变化的极佳解释，我建议去看《This is Phil Fish》[4]。既然这里是 HN，你们很多人大概知道 Phil Fish 和他的游戏《Fez》之间的那出闹剧，但那不重要，因为这支视频讲的是所有不是 Phil Fish 的人：那些提供投射、符号化代表和憎恨的受众——正是这些助燃了
comments.text: TL;DR - just watch [4] The internet has a serious problem with fame . Before the internet, fame was usually something that required an investment in media access . Everybody knows about the big Hollywood movie because they paid for a lot of advertising/etc. A low-budget film could potentially be more popular if people knew about it, but the meager (or nonexistent) advertising budget usually guaranteed it would never[1] become famous . This is what the internet changed. It's fundamental power is that anybody can publish because the network doesn't differentiate between "publishing" hosts and "consumer" hosts. All peers are supposed[2] to be equal in capability. The internet is media access. What used to require significant investment of time and/or money now happens to people regularly when they post something casually on the internet: they can become famous . Unfortunately, our social norms are still adapting to this change. As this article shows, trivial posts are incorrectly interpreted and the author ends up wading through flames and insults. This is because what started as a casual post is now addressing an audience . For a very good explanation of this type of change-in-relationship, I suggest watching "This is Phil Fish"[4]. As this is HN, many of you probably know the drama involving Phil Fish and his game "Fez", but tht doesn't matter because this video is about everybody who is not Phil Fish: the audience that supplies the projection, tokenism, and hatred that fuels

comments.author: pdkl95
comments.story_title: Curbs on free speech are growing tighter. It is time to speak out
comments.why_zh: 分析名声与网络暴民，讲的是除了 Phil Fish 之外的所有人。
comments.quote_zh: 我鼓励大家都去看 [1]，这样我们至少能清楚理解这个问题。
comments.text_zh: > 如果一个人有任何程度的社交媒体存在感，而且要么直言不讳，要么运气不好，那他们就有风险遭遇互联网暴民转而攻击他们。互联网最重要的特性之一，就是互联网本身就是媒体访问渠道。过去，“名气”是你主动投入并加入的东西。现在，名气会降临到你头上。你可能是在为你非正式地“混在一起”的同侪群体写作，但他们可以自发地转变成“一群观众”，带着（有时前后不一致的）期待。我们习惯了名气是你可以抽身离开的东西。如果你曾经投入其中，你总能回到自己的“正常生活”。摇滚明星可以放弃唱片合约，去做别的事情。新情况的问题在于，他们的“正常生活”正是名气的来源。如今要远离名气，就需要人们远离自己的正常生活。我不知道解决办法是什么——也许需要某种新的‘礼仪’——但对这个问题非常好的分析是视频论文《This Is Phil Fish》[1]。许多 HN 读者可能会认出这个名字是《Fez》的作者，但正如这篇论文开头提到的，“这是关于世界上所有不是 Phil Fish 的人”。我鼓励大家都去看 [1]，这样我们至少能清楚理解这个问题。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > if a person has any level of social media presence and they're either outspoken or unlucky then they risk an internet mob being turned against them. One of the most important properties of the internet is that the internet is media access. The concept of "fame" used to be something you bought into . Now, fame happens to you . You may be writing for the group of peers that you informally "hang out" with, but they can spontaneously transform into "an audience" that has (sometimes inconsistent) expectations. We're used top fame being something you can walk away from. If you bought into it, you can always go back to your "normal life". The rockstar can give up the record deals and do something else with their life. The problem with the new situation is that their "normal life" is the source of fame. To walk away from fame now requires people to walk away from their normal life . I don't know what the solution is - perhaps some new sort of 'etiquette' is needed - but a very good analysis of the problem is the video essay "This Is Phil Fish"[1]. May HN readers will recognize that name as the author of "Fez", but as the essay mentions at the beginning, "This is about everybody in the world who isn't Phil Fish". I encourage everyone to watch [1], so we at lest have a clear understanding of the problem. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: pdkl95
comments.story_title: Reasons YouTubers keep imploding, from a YouTuber
comments.why_zh: 解释互联网名气与传统名气的不同。
comments.quote_zh: 我强烈推荐观看 Innuendo Studios 的视频论文《This is Phil Fish》[1]。
comments.text_zh: 互联网改变了“名气”的本质。过去，你通常需要先投入名气这件事。要出名，你需要经纪人、公关人员等等。媒体访问渠道是一种有限资源，只发给那些获得认可的人。这在观众心中形成了关于出名意味着什么的某些期待。不要错待观众，也不要做任何太超出这些期待的事，否则就会面对观众的怒火。互联网改变了“出名”的含义，因为互联网就是媒体访问渠道。不幸的是，关于观众的社会学还没有跟上，而且常常仍然套用旧的期待。过去，抽身离开名气是可能的，因为它不是你的正常生活。出名是一份你（通常）可以离开的工作。然而，很多通过互联网出名的人无法离开。出名的是他们的正常生活。名气与个人生活之间的紧密耦合导致或放大了许多这类问题。要得到好得多的解释，我强烈推荐观看 Innuendo Studios 的视频论文《This is Phil Fish》[1]。尽管名字如此，它其实并不是关于 Phil Fish。它是关于所有不是 Phil Fish 的人，以及他们如何（错误地）处理互联网名人身份。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: The internet has changed the nature of "fame". In the past, you needed to generally buy into fame. To be famous, you needed managers, publicists, etc. Media access was a limited resource that was handed out only to those that met approval. This created in the audience certain expectations about what it means to be famous. Don't treat the audience wrong or do anything too far outside those expectations or face the audience's wrath. The internet changed what it means to be "famous" because the internet is media access . Unfortunately, the sociology of the audience hasn't caught up and often still apply the old expectations. In the past, it was possible to walk away from fame because it wasn't your normal life . Being famous was a job you could (usually) leave. However, a lot of people that have become famous through the internet cannot leave. It was their normal life that became famous. Tight coupling between fame and personal life causes or amplifies a lot of these problems. For a much better explanation, I highly recommend watching Innuendo Studios' video essay "This is Phil Fish"[1]. In spite of the name, it isn't really about Phil Fish. It's about everybody who isn't Phil Fish and how they (miss-)handle internet celebrity. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: pdkl95
comments.why_zh: 对互联网如何改变名气的最佳解释。
comments.quote_zh: 对这个问题最好的解释是 Innuendo Studios 的视频《This Is Phil Fish》[1]。
comments.text_zh:
> 有这样一种回应方式

这种应受谴责的回应会一直发生，直到社会最终明白互联网如何从根本上改变了名气的本质。对这个问题最好的解释是 Innuendo Studios 的视频《This Is Phil Fish》[1]。如果你还没看过，请去看。它讲的不是 Phil Fish；他只是一个用来说明互联网上名气如何运作的有用例子。请一定看这个视频！

核心问题在于，名气过去是自愿选择加入的。出名需要基础设施。要获得这些基础设施，需要得到各种守门人的许可、时间和资源。你必须努力才能出名，因为媒体渠道是稀缺资源。在互联网上，名气变成了发生在你身上的事，因为互联网本身就是媒体渠道。我们习惯于把名气看作一种选择；如果你不想出名，你可以离开媒体基础设施，回到你的“正常生活”。有名的乐队可以停止巡演。现在每个人都有媒体渠道，那种“正常生活”可以直接变得有名。当这发生时，离开名气就意味着离开你的正常生活。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > there’s this style of response This type of reprehensible response will keep happening until society finally learns how the internet fundamentally changed the nature of fame . The best explanation of the problem is the video "This Is Phil Fish"[1] by Innuendo Studios. If you haven't seen it, please watch it. It's not about Phil Fish; he is simply a useful example of how fame works on the internet. Please watch the video! The core problem is that fame used to be opt-in . Becoming famous required infrastructure. Gaining access to that infrastructure required the permission various gatekeepers, time, and resources. You had to work to become famous, because media access was a scarce resource. On the internet fame became something that happens to you , because the internet IS media access. We're used to seeing fame as something that was chosen ; if you didn't want to be famous, you could walk away from the media infrastructure and go back to your "normal life". The famous band could quit touring. Now that everyone has media access, that "normal life" can become famous directly. When that happens, walking away from fame means walking away from your normal life . [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: pdkl95
comments.story_title: Naomi Wu video demonetized on YouTube
comments.why_zh: 解释了互联网如何改变成名机制。
comments.quote_zh: 可能是 YouTube 上最重要的视频——是 Innuendo Studios 的《This Is Phil Fish》[1]。
comments.text_zh: 虽然有些人确实似乎认同“觉得自己的男子气概/世界观受到威胁”这种解释，但很多人似乎并不理解的根本问题是，互联网改变了成名的机制。我见过的最好的解释——也可能是 YouTube 上最重要的视频——是 Innuendo Studios 的《This Is Phil Fish》[1]。它其实不是关于 Phil Fish 的；它是关于所有不是 Phil Fish 的人，在决定他变得“出名”时是如何行动的。过去，要“上电视”“组乐队”或其他传统意义上的出名，多少需要你主动买账、接受成名这件事。想出名需要媒体渠道，而这些渠道由守门人控制。如果你想“上电视”之类的，就得和这些守门人合作；而正因为你必须选择参与，人们常常把决定成名也看作接受了某种责任，要“按名流该有的样子行事”。互联网从根本上改变了成名的机制，因为互联网本身就是媒体渠道。现在，你只要在正常的日常生活中做自己，就有可能出名——成为“名人”，并背负以某种方式行事的“责任”。 [1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: While some people certainly seem to subscribe to "feeling their masculinity/world-view is threatened" interpretation, the fundamental problem that q lot of people don't seem to understand is that the internet changed the mechanics of fame . The best explanation I've seen - and possibly the most important video on youtube - is "This Is Phil Fish"[1] by Innuendo Studios. It's not really about Phil Fish; it's about everyone who isn't Phil Fish acted when they decided he became "famous". In the past, being "on tv" or "in a band" or other traditional examples of fame required some amount of buying into fame. Becoming famous required media access that was controlled by gatekeepers. You had to work with those gatekeepers if you wanted to be "on tv" or whatever, and because you had to choose to participate, people often see the decision to become famous as also accepting some amount of responsibility to "act like famous people are supposed to act". This internet fundamentally changed the mechanics of fame, because the internet IS media access . Now it is possible to become famous - to become a "celebrity" with a "responsibility" to act in a certain way - simply by being yourself in your normal everyday life. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: dcolgan
comments.story_title: No Man’s Sky One Year Later
comments.why_zh: 关于 Phil Fish 失宠的深度视频。
comments.quote_zh: 有人做了一个非常深入的视频，讲《Fez》的创作者 Phil Fish 的失宠
comments.text_zh: 作为一名前业余 Twitch.tv 主播，我一直对互联网人物的兴衰很着迷，而一些最大的互联网人物似乎是那些被推到聚光灯下的游戏开发者。有人做了一个非常深入的视频，讲《Fez》的创作者 Phil Fish 的失宠：[VIDEO] 在我看来，高压、一个好斗的性格，再加上互联网匿名性，组合成了一个非常混乱的局面，把他逼出了这个行业。我也关注过 Narscissa（原名 Cosmo）Wright 在出柜为跨性别者之后在速通社区的余波。她曾是 Twitch 上最受欢迎的主播之一，我想变性别已经够难了，而在由匿名玩家组成的演播室观众面前变性别，那会是另一个层级。Sean Murray 和《No Man's Sky》似乎也是如此。缺乏经验，加上过度承诺和极高的期待，造成了当前的局面。我不认为这些人中有谁心怀恶意，我也不知道自己会建议他们怎么做得不一样。Edmund McMillen，《Super Meat Boy》和其他独立游戏的创作者，曾在一次播客采访中说，正是因为这个原因，他讨厌在作品完成前给别人看。编辑：我知道这些人的情况并不完全相同，我只是呼吁多一些理解和共情，而不是把每个人都往最坏处想。
comments.text: As a former amateur Twitch.tv streamer, I've always been fascinated by the rise and fall of internet personalities, and some of the biggest personalities seem to be game developers that found themselves in the spotlight. Someone made this very in-depth video about the fall from grace of Phil Fish, the creator of Fez: [VIDEO] It seems to me that the combo of high pressure and a guy with a combative personality combined with internet anonymity to create a really messy situation that drove him out of the business. I've also followed Narscissa (formerly Cosmo) Wright's fallout in the speedrun community after coming out as transgender. Once one of the most popular streamers on Twitch, I'd imagine transitioning is hard enough, but transitioning in front of a studio audience of anonymous gamers would be next level. And so the same seems to be with Sean Murray and No Man's Sky. Inexperience plus overpromising and really high expectations created the current situation. I don't think any of these people are malicious and I don't really know how I would have advised them to do things differently. Edmund McMillen, the creator of Super Meat Boy and other indie games once said in a podcast interview that he hates showing people what he's making before it is done for this very reason. Edit: I know the circumstances of these people are not identical, I'm just calling for more understanding and empathy instead of assuming the worst in everyone.

comments.why_zh: 解释了名气如今如何主动降临到你身上。
comments.quote_zh: 关于这个话题的很好解释，我推荐这个[1]视频。
comments.text_zh: 名气过去是你必须去争取的东西，因为出名需要接触有限的基础设施。媒体渠道是稀缺的，所以你必须努力才能被那些基础设施的守门人注意到。数字通信和网络互联从根本上改变了这一点；发布内容的成本降到了几乎为零。基本的媒体渠道实际上不再稀缺。你不再需要讨好守门人，因为比如你可以免费发一条推文。这意味着现在有可能意外触达比大多数前互联网时代媒体大得多的受众。名气现在成了一种可能发生在你身上的事。更糟的是，传统观念里的名气是你可以转身离开的东西。你只要退出参与就行；作为某种名人是一份需要维护的工作。当你在 Twitter 等平台上意外出名时，往往是你正常的生活碰巧出了名。离开它，就意味着离开你的正常生活。关于这个话题的很好解释，我推荐这个[1]视频。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Fame used to be something you had to ask for, because being famous required access to limited infrastructure. Media access was scarce , and so you had to work to be noticed by the gatekeepers of that infrastructure. Digital communication an internetworking fundamentally changed that; the cost to publish dropped to approximately zero. Basic media access is de facto no longer scarce. You no longer need to appeal to a gatekeeper when you can e.g. post a tweet for free. This means it it now possible to accidentally reach a much larger audience than the most of the pre-internet media. Fame is now something that can happen to you. Worse, the traditional idea of fame was something you could walk away form. You simply quit participating; being some type of celebrity was a job that required maintenance. When you become accidentally famous on Twitter/etc it is often your normal life that happened to become famous. Walking away form that means walking away from your normal life. For a very good explanation of this topic, I recommend this[1] video. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: pdkl95
comments.why_zh: 关于互联网如何改变名气的短视频论文。
comments.quote_zh: 想看更好的解释，请看这个[1]短视频论文。
comments.text_zh: 这种有问题的准社会关系会被互联网放大，因为互联网改变了名气的运作机制。过去，出名需要基础设施。媒体渠道是稀缺的；如果你想获得出名的机会，就必须主动与各种守门人打交道。这通常需要戴上观众想看到的面具。摘下面具、退回你的“正常生活”很容易：如果没有定期维护，对媒体基础设施的使用权就会转到别人手里。在互联网上，任何人都可以在任何时候出名，因为互联网本身就是媒体渠道。人们现在不需要那副把名人形象与正常生活区分开的面具也能出名。现在放弃名气，意味着放弃你正常生活中那部分让你出名的东西。想看更好的解释，请看这个[1]短视频论文。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: This type of problematic parasocial relationship is amplified by the internet, because the internet changed the mechanics of fame . In the past, becoming famous required infrastructure . Media access was scarce; you had to actively work with various gatekeepers if you wanted the opportunity to become famous. This often required putting on the mask the audience wanted to see. Removing the mask and retreating back to your "normal life" was easy: without regular upkeep, access to the media infrastructure moved to someone else. On the internet, anybody can become famous at any time, because the internet is media access . People now become famous without the mask that differentiated their famous persona from their normal life. Giving up fame now requires giving up the part of your normal life that made you famous. For a much better explanation, see this[1] short video essay. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text: The internet has changed the concept of "fame". In the past, being famous usually required a lot of effort and (usually) money. Many people that could have been famous but didn't spend the time/money to make it happen were often discovered by the larger public only after their death . The end game of this property are things like the modern manufactured artist, where fame is achieved because that was the business plan. An important consequence of this "traditional" type of fame is that someone who wants to leave and get their old life back can generally stop participating. Without the time/money investment the public moves on. "Traditional" fame is a job you can walk away from. This changed with the internet, where people can become famous by accident . A tweet or blog post can suddenly get millions of views, or something you made can suddenly become the thing that everybody is trying to get a copy of. It's obvious that this is a well-known concept because we have entire industries working to try to make their product "go viral". This "unexpected" type of fame has a serious problem: it's permanent . It is hard or impossible to simply "walk away' from something when that would mean walking away from your normal life . When the tsunami of unexpected fame suddenly happens to someone, it is perfectly rational for someone to try to escape the situation before it becomes permanent. comments.text: I think you've got cause and effect reversed—GamerGate worked because gamers were already prone to this sort of behavior. See "This is Phil Fish," [1] a video (by the same person who did the GamerGate video) about Phil Fish, the creator of the acclaimed indie game "Fez." He was driven off the Internet (or at least out of public participation) by similar toxic behavior. Phil Fish is a white male. I don't know how long this has been going on, and it does seem to be getting steadily worse, but I don't think GamerGate was a turning point. Just a particularly visible example of how bad things have gotten. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 有人做了一个非常深入的视频，讲《Fez》的创作者 Phil Fish 的失宠：[VIDEO] 这个视频让我不舒服。我并非不同意它。事实上，我第一次看的时候，觉得它和本人对 Fish 的看法相当相似。也许只是和我的感受差了几度。大约三年后第一次重看，让我意识到它为什么让我不舒服。视频和我的观点之间的差异，正是如果我想发表关于这个话题的强有力的个人论证并被认真对待时，我会做的那组改动。Fish 是一个有趣的案例研究：一个互联网无名之辈变成名人，却没能很好地适应人们现在会在意他说的话这一事实。这个视频打磨掉的粗糙边缘以及所做的方便省略，正是我会对自己的观点做出的调整，以保住自己在游戏回音室中的可信度。
comments.text: Someone made this very in-depth video about the fall from grace of Phil Fish, the creator of Fez: [VIDEO] This video bugs me. I don't disagree with it. In fact, the first time I watched it, I found it quite similar to my own take on Fish. Maybe just a few degrees off of how I feel. Watching it for the first time in ~three years made me realize why it bugged me. The differences between the video and my opinions are the set of changes I'd make if I wanted to publish the strong argument for my perspective on the topic and be taken seriously. Fish is an interesting case study of internet-rando-turned-celebrity that doesn't adapt well to the fact people now care what he's saying. The rough edges sanded and convenient omissions made by this video are the exact same tweaks I'd make to my perspective to hold onto my own credibility in the games echo chamber.
